blocks.prompt: 13 A company starts with an initial inventory of 1,000 items. Each month, the company restocks 100 items and expects inventory costs to grow at 2% per month due to inflation. Use the binomial theorem to estimate the inventory cost after 6 months.
blocks.explanation:
Two things change: the number of items (+100 per month) and the cost of each item (\(\times 1.02\) per month).
The question gives no price per item, so the answer is the cost as a multiple of today's price \(c\) of one item.
Plan: items after 6 months; growth factor \((1.02)^6\) by the binomial theorem; multiply.
steps:
Given: 1000 items at the start; +100 items each month; cost grows 2% = 0.02 per month; time 6 months.
To find: the estimated inventory cost after 6 months.
Method: Let \(c\) be today's cost of one item. After 6 months the cost of one item is \(c(1 + 0.02)^6\); estimate \((1.02)^6\) by the binomial theorem. Then cost = (number of items) \(\times\) (new cost of one item).

Number of items after 6 months
\[1000 + 6 \times 100 = 1600 \text{ items}\]
Why: 100 items are added in each of the 6 months.

Growth factor of the cost
\[(1 + 0.02)^6 = 1 + 6(0.02) + 15(0.02)^2\]
\[+ 20(0.02)^3 + \dots\]
Why: 2% growth per month multiplies the cost by 1.02 each month. Row 6 of Pascal's triangle: 1, 6, 15, 20, 15, 6, 1.

Estimate the cost
\[\text{Cost} \approx 1600 \times 1.126\,c\]
\[= 1801.6\,c\]
Why: Each of the 1600 items now costs about \(1.126c\). (We value the whole stock at the month-6 price, as the question asks for the cost after 6 months.)

Check:
\[(1.02)^6 = 1.126162\ldots\]
\[1600 \times 1.126162 = 1801.86\]
Why: The exact factor differs from our estimate only in the 4th decimal place.
blocks.final_answer: After 6 months there are 1600 items and the cost is about \(1.126\) times today's cost of 1600 items, that is \(\approx 1801.6\,c\) (\(c\) = today's cost of one item). For example, at Rs. 100 per item today this is about Rs. 180,160.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints "180,160 items". The stock after 6 months is 1600 items, not 180,160. The figure \(180{,}160 = 1600 \times 1.126 \times 100\) is a cost in rupees, and only if one item costs Rs. 100 today, which the question does not state.
